message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most famous American composers across different eras and genres:

| Composer | Lifespan | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|----------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris* | Blended jazz with classical forms; helped popularize “American” classical music. |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* | Known as the “Dean of American composers”; his music evokes the American landscape. |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | *West Side Story*, *Candide* | Renowned conductor, pianist, and composer; bridged Broadway and symphonic worlds. |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* | One of the most celebrated film composers worldwide. |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist works such as *Glassworks*, *Einstein on the Beach* | Pioneered minimalism in contemporary classical music. |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* | Known for lyrical, emotionally resonant compositions. |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* | Early modernist who incorporated American folk tunes into classical structures. |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird* | First African American to have a symphony performed by a major orchestra. |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* | Contemporary composer known for postminimalist style. |
| **Elliott Carter** (1908–2012) | *Variations on a Theme of Frank Bridge*, *Music for Piano and Orchestra* | Advanced modernist techniques; highly respected in academic circles. |

These composers span a range of styles—from early 20th‑century modernism to contemporary minimalism—and have left indelible marks on both American and global music scenes.
